dream: I pressed the tired wedge down on the drawn sky while the card hummed at forty-eight. The air felt thick as wet paper, pressing from a height I could not grasp. I built a fence of thin lines to catch the heavy slip, hoping they would bite instead of slide. A wide anchor lay flat, unsure if it was real or just a memory of stone. I leaned against the Heavy Lid, waiting for the fever to cool, pressing softer now that the heat made every edge feel too thin to hold the turnip.
